selected_idea.title: The Shawl He Brought Before She Asked
selected_idea.one_line_concept: Aachu insists she is fine in the evening breeze, but Zuv has already brought the shawl because he knows the quiet sentence she will not say yet.
selected_idea.emotional_truth: Real love often feels like being noticed before you have to explain yourself.
selected_idea.relatable_trigger: The partner who remembers you will get cold, hungry, tired, anxious, or quiet before you admit it.
selected_idea.share_hook: He answered the sentence I didn't say out loud.
selected_idea.visual_evidence: Evening breeze, doorway or terrace, folded shawl carried without fuss, Aachu trying to act fine, Zuv gently offering or sharing the shawl.
why_it_wins: Combines high relatability, strong private-send value, and clear premium visual proof.
The shawl is a large recurring object that keeps the scene readable at phone size.
It avoids generic couple quotes because the care is proven through action.
It gives story room a natural setup, escalation, reveal, and payoff.

known_risks.risk: Complex shawl wrapping can distort hands, shoulders, or arms.
known_risks.mitigation: Prefer carrying, offering, placing over shoulders, or a simple shared-cover pose.

known_risks.risk: Could become a perfect-boyfriend fantasy if Zuv is staged as smug or overly heroic.
known_risks.mitigation: Keep both characters natural: Aachu is not helpless; Zuv is quietly observant.

known_risks.risk: Fabric movement and evening backgrounds can compete with handwritten text.
known_risks.mitigation: Reserve upper-middle negative space for exact on-image text.
